history.value: Headline began in 1997 in Santa Barbara as Bertelsmann Ventures, an internet fund, and became BV Capital in 2000, with Mathias Schilling and Thomas Gieselmann among its founders, then e.ventures in 2012 and Headline in 2021. It became known for bets on Sonos, Farfetch, Bumble and Mistral AI. Today it runs early stage funds for the US, Europe, Asia and Brazil and a global growth fund, the largest of which closed at $865 million in 2024.
history.basis: Founding and names: Wikipedia 'Headline (company)' (Bertelsmann Ventures 1997 in Santa Barbara, founded by Jan Henric Buettner and Wolfgang Rose; BV Capital 2000 with Buettner, Rose, Mathias Schilling and Thomas Gieselmann; e.ventures 2012; Headline 2021) and TechCrunch 2012-07-15 on the e.ventures rename. Bets: Sonos (BV Capital, 2005), Farfetch, Bumble (growth fund, 2020), Mistral AI (seed, 2023), all members of the portfolio on this page. Latest fund: Headline Global Growth IV at $865M (Fortune 2024-09-18, https://fortune.com/2024/09/18/headline-raises-865-million-hires-new-head-of-growth/). Moved to this sidecar to fit the shape rule: the move from Santa Barbara to San Francisco; offices in Berlin, Hamburg, Paris and London; the Asia desk (Infinity Ventures, now Headline Asia, own fund family, out of the portfolio on this page, decisions.md D2) and the Brazil desk (Redpoint eventures, later Headline Brazil, out, D3); US VII $408M and EU VII EUR 320M (TechCrunch 2022-07-07); the firm's early check of $1.5M to $15M. Revised 2026-09-28 for Erik's E1 (the Asia and Brazil desks in): the desks now read in the third sentence; BV Capital's founders were Jan Henric Buettner, Wolfgang Rose, Mathias Schilling and Thomas Gieselmann (Wikipedia).

investment_concept.value: “Global venture capital helping founders win, bigger.”
investment_concept.basis: The firm's own line, read 2026-09-27: the homepage carries no headline element (a rotating highlights strip opens with 'Over 25 years, it's been our honor to work alongside exceptional founders.'), so the title-tag tagline stands: 'Headline | Global Venture Capital Helping Founders Win, Bigger', set in sentence case with one closing period. Competing lines on the same page: the section title 'A boutique firm with global wingspan.'; the meta description 'Headline is a global venture capital firm with teams across the US, Europe, Asia, and Brazil. ...'; the footer 'Headline is a venture capital firm with dedicated teams on the ground around the world.' Published inside quotation marks, as the firm's own words (Erik, 2026-09-26).

investment_stage.basis: The firm's own statement: it invests 'from software and AI applications to consumer and fintech, and lead rounds at every stage' (meta description), with early funds per region and a global growth fund (fund pages US, EU, Global Growth). The landed entry distribution over the members is Series A 107, Seed 87, Growth 59, Pre-Seed 3, desks included (restated in report.md).

investment_geo.basis: From the members' headquarters at the rebuild of 2026-09-28, after Erik's E1 brought the Asia and Brazil desks in (386 nameable rows): US 152, Europe 111 (Germany 32, UK 25, France 17, Russia 10, Denmark 6, others 21), Latin America 61 (Brazil 59, Chile, Colombia), Asia 53 (Japan 26, China 12, Taiwan 6, Singapore 4, Malaysia 2, Hong Kong, Vietnam, South Korea), Israel 4, Australia 2, Canada 2, New Zealand 1. Core US and Europe (two-label cap), other Latin America and Asia, matching the firm's four early fund families.

investment_range.basis: MEDIAN: $7.6M, published as $8M, the median entry round over the 248 members whose entry round is on record with an amount, the desks included (the firm's own posts and press, else the entry Form D; non-USD at the ECB rate of the round's date: p10 $2.0M, p25 $4.0M, p75 $17.0M, p90 $30.0M; before the desks came in, $10.0M over 158); Form D alone covers only 29 members because two thirds of the portfolio is European or pre-2009, so the median is press-based (the Creandum recipe). It is a round size, not a cheque size. LOWER: the firm's stated early check, '$1.5 million to $15 million per startup' (TechCrunch 2022-07-07). UPPER: the largest round the firm led, Fonoa's $110M Series C (2026-05-28, https://blog.headline.com/p/fonoa-the-ai-operating-system-global), 12.7% of the $865M Global Growth IV, inside the 10 to 15% single-position check; next: Cameo's $100M Series C led by e.ventures (2021), Homa's $100M Series B co-led (2022). Aggregator 'typical check' figures were not used.

notable_investments.basis: The five best known of the firm's own companies, most recognised first (PRO-152, Erik 2026-09-24). Considered next: The RealReal, Gopuff, Cameo, Segment, Bird, Acorns, Flutterwave. Mistral is published as the firm's own site names it (the portfolio row's name); sibling books publish 'Mistral AI'.

Added with the desks (Erik's E1, 2026-09-28): Headline Asia V $145M (TechCrunch 2025-05-19, https://techcrunch.com/2025/05/19/headline-asias-145m-fund-v-is-first-new-significant-vc-fund-raised-in-months/); Headline Brazil III R$915M = $169.4M at the ECB rate of 2022-07-07 (BRL/EUR 5.4983, EUR/USD 1.018; TechCrunch 2022-07-07); Headline Asia IV 'over $100 million' (Headline Asia's release, 2021-08-03, https://macaubusiness.com/headline-asia-announces-the-close-of-fund-4-at-over-100-million/), listed at its floor; Redpoint eventures I $130M (TechCrunch 2012-07-23, the joint fund with Redpoint Ventures).
